content.title: THE DAILY {{NUMBERS}} CHEAT SHEET NOBODY GAVE YOU
facts: **Cold shower** -> 30 seconds at the end -> Sharper, more awake
**Sunlight** -> 10 min before 9am -> Steadier mood all day
**Deep breathing** -> 5 slow breaths -> Lowers stress fast
**Water** -> 500 ml right after waking -> Kickstarts your metabolism
**Stretching** -> 3 minutes before bed -> Fewer nighttime cramps
**Grip strength** -> 20 seconds squeezing a ball -> Calms a racing mind
**Sleep** -> 7-9 hours, same bedtime -> Sharper memory next day
**Journaling** -> 3 things written down -> Less nighttime overthinking
**Nature time** -> 20 minutes outside -> Drops cortisol noticeably
**Follow along** – for more daily habits that quietly add up.
content.caption:
A few of these are worth slowing down on. That 500 ml of water right after waking works because you're mildly dehydrated after 7-8 hours of no fluids, and your metabolism actually runs sluggish until you rehydrate. Sunlight before 9am isn't just "nice" - early light exposure helps set your circadian rhythm, which is directly tied to how stable your mood and energy feel later that day. And grip strength squeezing, weirdly, activates your parasympathetic nervous system through the tension-release pattern, which is why it can calm a racing mind faster than just "trying to relax." Everyone's body responds a little differently, so treat these as starting points, not strict rules.
